messages.subject: Fitting a simple GP -- Cholesky issue?
parts:
Hi list. Louis and I are working on a GP model with Andrew for survey
responses and we came across something unexpected, wanted to see if
anyone knew what was going on, whether Stan was suppressing a relevant
error message or something else. Attached is a minimal working example
of a GP with Binomial observation model.

We're just using a dot product covariance function (k(x,x') = <x,x'> +
c) for the GP prior. We were expecting that this prior would give us
straight lines, as in my Shiny demo here (since it has a closed form
solution, I coded this up with a normal observation model, but for the
posterior mean it's pretty much equivalent):
https://flaxter.shinyapps.io/linearkernel/

Due to numerical issues (I think) it's not working in Stan, which you
can see if you run the code attached. Plot here:
https://www.dropbox.com/s/48l0n7021g5tv16/plot1.png?dl=0

All it takes to fix it is to add some noise to the main diagonal. Plot
here: https://www.dropbox.com/s/hpcnfqew1o303si/plot2.png?dl=0

No big deal now that I realize it, I'm just wondering what Stan did
when it took the cholesky decomposition, whether it was silently
having issues or what? Switching to y ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma) gives
me the following when there's no extra noise on the main diagonal:

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be
rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::multi_normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): LDLT_Factor of
covariance parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite.
LDLT_Factor of covariance parameterlast conditional variance is
-3.46945e-018:0.
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained
variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either
severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.
Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.


Thoughts?
Seth

messages.subject: Re: Fitting a simple GP -- Cholesky issue?
parts:
On Friday, October 31, 2014 2:59:49 PM UTC-4, Seth Flaxman wrote:
No big deal now that I realize it, I'm just wondering what Stan did
when it took the cholesky decomposition, whether it was silently
having issues or what? Switching to y ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma) gives
me the following when there's no extra noise on the main diagonal:

The multi_normal_choleksy() function trusts that L is a valid Cholesky factor, whereas multi_normal() checks that the covariance matrix is positive definite, which is numerically unstable. So, the former is better to use when you know that the covariance matrix is positive definite by construction.

Ben
